Load the libraries

library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(ggmap)
library(leaflet)

API Key

register_stadiamaps("0705cbb2-b9b7-400c-a5b7-d5689775e80e", write = FALSE)

Load the Data

For this homework, we will use the shark attack data to visualize where the attacks occurred. The data are from: State of California- Shark Incident Database.

nsharks <- read_csv("data/SharkIncidents_1950_2022_220302.csv") %>% 
  clean_names() %>% 
  filter(longitude !="NA" & latitude !="NA") %>% # pulling out NA locations
  mutate(longitude = as.numeric(longitude)) # converting longitude to numeric
  1. Use the range of the latitude and longitude to build an appropriate bounding box for your map.
nsharks %>%
  select(latitude, longitude) %>%
  summary()
##     latitude       longitude     
##  Min.   :32.59   Min.   :-124.7  
##  1st Qu.:34.04   1st Qu.:-123.1  
##  Median :36.70   Median :-122.0  
##  Mean   :36.36   Mean   :-121.4  
##  3rd Qu.:38.18   3rd Qu.:-119.6  
##  Max.   :41.56   Max.   :-117.1
lat <- c(32.59, 41.56)
long <-  c(-124.7, -117.1)
bbox <- make_bbox(long, lat, f=0.03)
  1. Load a map from stamen in a terrain style projection and display the map.
map1 <- get_stadiamap(bbox, maptype = "stamen_terrain", zoom=7)
## ℹ © Stadia Maps © Stamen Design © OpenMapTiles © OpenStreetMap contributors.
ggmap(map1)

  1. Build a map that overlays the recorded observations of shark attacks in California.
ggmap(map1) +
  geom_point(data=nsharks, aes(longitude, latitude), size=0.75,
             color="gray29", alpha=0.8)+
  labs(x="Longitude", y="latitude", title = "Where da sharks at")

  1. Build a map that only shows the fatalities.
fsharks <- sharks <- read_csv("data/SharkIncidents_1950_2022_220302.csv") %>%
  clean_names() %>% 
  filter(longitude !="NA" & latitude !="NA" & injury=="fatal") %>% 
  mutate(longitude = as.numeric(longitude))
## Rows: 211 Columns: 16
## ── Column specification ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Delimiter: ","
## chr (12): IncidentNum, Time, County, Location, Mode, Injury, Depth, Species,...
## dbl  (4): Month, Day, Year, Latitude
## 
## ℹ Use `spec()` to retrieve the full column specification for this data.
## ℹ Specify the column types or set `show_col_types = FALSE` to quiet this message.
fsharks %>%
  select(longitude, latitude) %>%
  summary()
##    longitude         latitude    
##  Min.   :-123.8   Min.   :32.85  
##  1st Qu.:-122.2   1st Qu.:34.36  
##  Median :-120.9   Median :35.40  
##  Mean   :-120.9   Mean   :35.60  
##  3rd Qu.:-120.7   3rd Qu.:36.77  
##  Max.   :-117.3   Max.   :39.58
flat <- c(32.85, 39.58)
flong <- c(-123.8, -117.3)
bbox <- make_bbox(flong, flat, f=0.03)
map2 <- get_stadiamap(bbox, maptype = "stamen_terrain", zoom=7)
## ℹ © Stadia Maps © Stamen Design © OpenMapTiles © OpenStreetMap contributors.
ggmap(map1) +
  geom_point(data=fsharks, aes(longitude, latitude), size=0.75,
             color="red3", alpha=0.8)+
  labs(x="Longitude", y="latitude", title = "Where Jaws could have reasonably been shot at")

  1. Build the same map (fatalities only), but this time make it interactive using leaflet. Also, color the points red.
lon_min <- -123.8 
lon_max <- -117.3
lat_min <- 32.85
lat_max <- 39.58
leaflet(fsharks) %>%
  addProviderTiles(providers$Stadia.StamenTerrain) %>%
  addCircleMarkers(
    lng = ~longitude,
    lat = ~latitude,
    radius = 2,
    stroke = FALSE,
    fillOpacity=.9
  ) %>%
  addScaleBar(position = "bottomleft" ) %>%
  fitBounds(lng1=lon_min, lat1= lat_min,
            lng2=lon_max, lat2 = lat_max)
  1. Which county has the highest number of recorded shark attacks? Make a map that only shows the attacks in this county. (hint: it may help improve the map if you remove duplicate locations, i.e. multiple attacks at the same location.)
nsharks %>%
  count(county)

  #San Diego has the highest number of recorded shark attacks
Dsharks <- read_csv("data/SharkIncidents_1950_2022_220302.csv") %>% 
  clean_names() %>% 
  filter(longitude !="NA" & latitude !="NA" & county=="San Diego") %>% 
  mutate(longitude = as.numeric(longitude))
## Rows: 211 Columns: 16
## ── Column specification ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Delimiter: ","
## chr (12): IncidentNum, Time, County, Location, Mode, Injury, Depth, Species,...
## dbl  (4): Month, Day, Year, Latitude
## 
## ℹ Use `spec()` to retrieve the full column specification for this data.

Dsharks %>%
  select(longitude, latitude) %>%
  summary()
##    longitude         latitude    
##  Min.   :-118.1   Min.   :32.59  
##  1st Qu.:-117.6   1st Qu.:32.77  
##  Median :-117.4   Median :32.85  
##  Mean   :-117.5   Mean   :32.97  
##  3rd Qu.:-117.3   3rd Qu.:33.23  
##  Max.   :-117.1   Max.   :33.37
Dlon_min <- -118.1 
Dlon_max <- -117.1
Dlat_min <- 32.59
Dlat_max <- 33.37
leaflet(fsharks) %>%
  addProviderTiles(providers$Stadia.StamenTerrain) %>%
  addCircleMarkers(
    lng = ~longitude,
    lat = ~latitude,
    radius = 2,
    stroke = FALSE,
    fillOpacity=.9
  ) %>%
  addScaleBar(position = "bottomleft" ) %>%
  fitBounds(lng1=Dlon_min, lat1= Dlat_min,
            lng2=Dlon_max, lat2 = Dlat_max)
